travelAdvisory.summary:
Exercise increased cautionin Germany due to terrorism.
Terrorist groups and lone actors remain a constant threat in Germany and Europe, attacking people in public locations with knives, small arms, rudimentary explosive devices, and vehicles.  Such attacks may occur with little or no warning and target:  

Tourist locations 
Transportation centers (airports, train, or bus stations)  
Markets and shopping malls 
Local government facilities 
Hotels, clubs, and restaurants 
Places of worship and ed

healthcare.systemType: Universal (Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung / GKV — statutory health insurance, mandatory for residents)
healthcare.costForTourists: System: Universal (Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung / GKV — statutory health insurance, mandatory for residents) Quality: ★★★★★ (5/5) One of the best healthcare systems in the world. Highly trained doctors, excellent hospitals. English is commonly spoken in medical settings in major cities. Wait times are generally short. Everyone pays for health insurance — even tourists should have coverage. 💡 Medical Tourism Germany is a top destination for medical tourism, particularly for cancer treatment, cardiovascular procedures, and orthopedics. High quality, moderate costs compared to the US.
healthcare.hospitalNotes: Access: easy Hours: Most pharmacies open 8:30am-6:30pm weekdays, 9am-4pm Saturdays. Some pharmacies in major cities have late-night hours. An 'Apothekennotdienst' (emergency pharmacy) is always available nearby — check online or ask any pharmacy for the nearest on-duty pharmacy. Prescription rules: EU prescriptions are accepted. Non-EU prescriptions require a German doctor's verification. Germany has strict prescription rules — many antibiotics and medications require a prescription. 💡 Tips Pharmacies (Apotheke) are widely available. Most medications require a prescription. Pharmacists are highly trained and can advise on minor ailments. Look for the red 'A' sign.

vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for travelers. FSME vaccination is recommended if visiting rural/forested areas in spring/summer.

water.notes: Tap water is safe to drink throughout Germany. Germany has some of the best drinking water quality in the world.

healthcare.foodSafetyTips: Excellent food safety standards. German cuisine is hearty — be aware of rich foods, pork, and sauerkraut if your stomach isn't used to them. Raw minced meat (Mett) is popular — it's safe from reputable sources. Cheese and dairy are generally safe. Watch out for pork-heavy dishes.

travelInsurance.requiredNote: Not legally required for short stays, but strongly recommended. EU citizens should carry EHIC/GHIC.

healthcare.qualityNotes: One of the best healthcare systems in the world. Highly trained doctors, excellent hospitals. English is commonly spoken in medical settings in major cities. Wait times are generally short. Everyone pays for health insurance — even tourists should have coverage.

medications.generalAdvice: Germany follows strict EU/Schengen rules for medication imports. Travelers from Schengen countries must carry a Schengen medical certificate (Schengen-Bescheinigung) for narcotics. Non-Schengen travelers need a doctor's attestation certified by the health authority of their country. The Federal Institute for Drugs and Medical Devices (BfArM) oversees controlled substances.

controlledSubstances.note: Germany partially legalized cannabis in April 2024 for personal use (up to 25g in public). However, importing cannabis from abroad remains illegal. Medical cannabis requires a German prescription. Do not bring cannabis products into Germany.
Controlled under the German Narcotics Act (BtMG). Requires Schengen certificate for Schengen travelers or certified doctor's attestation for others. Maximum 30 days' supply.

Strictly controlled. Adderall (mixed amphetamine salts) is NOT approved in Germany. Methylphenidate (Ritalin/Medikinet) is available with prescription. Requires Schengen certificate or BfArM import permit. Apply well before travel.
Controlled under BtMG. Requires proper documentation — Schengen certificate or doctor's attestation. Maximum 30 days' supply in original packaging.
Classified as narcotics under BtMG. Possession and import without medical prescription is a criminal offense.

The photos look real, the host is communicative, and they want a deposit transferred before you arrive. Then you show up and either the apartment doesn't exist or it's nothing li...

scams.name: The Shell Game Street Hustle
scams.description: You notice a small crowd gathered around a man doing a quick three-cup shuffle game on a folding table. A few spectators seem to win easily, and the dealer looks friendly and casual. You decide to try your luck — except the game is completely rigged. The 'winners' in the crowd are all plants (shills) hired to lure you in. The ball is moved by sleight of hand after you place your bet. No tourist ever wins. Some people have lost €50-100 in minutes thinking they spotted the pattern.
scams.avoidance: Never gamble on the street — it's always rigged | The 'winners' you see are all working with the dealer | Just keep walking and don't engage

connectivity.simOptions: Prepaid SIMs from Telekom (best coverage), Vodafone, or O2 at airports, Saturn/MediaMarkt stores, and supermarkets. ~€15-30 for 10-25GB. eSIM via Airalo or Holafly from $5 USD. Note: registration required for SIM (passport needed).
connectivity.wifiAvailability: WiFi ubiquitous at hotels, cafes, and restaurants. Train stations have free WiFi. Deutsche Bahn trains have WiFi (variable quality). Public free WiFi exists in many city centers.
connectivity.bestOption: Telekom or Vodafone prepaid SIM for best LTE/5G coverage. Buy at Frankfurt or Munich airport on arrival, or at a MediaMarkt electronics store.

cultural.tipping: Round up restaurant bills or leave 5-10% for good service — tell the server the total you want to pay when settling. Don't leave cash on the table. Tip taxi drivers 5-10% by rounding up. Not obligatory but appreciated.
cultural.dressCode: Practical and understated. Germans dress for function. Smart casual for restaurants. No shorts or flip-flops in upscale venues. Business attire is formal.
cultural.greetings: Firm handshake, direct eye contact. 'Guten Morgen/Tag/Abend' (Good morning/day/evening). Last-name basis with Herr/Frau until invited to use first names. Punctuality is extremely important.
taboos: Being late — punctuality is considered basic respect in Germany
Jaywalking — Germans wait for the light even on empty roads
Making Nazi references or jokes — illegal and deeply offensive
Talking loudly in public spaces, especially public transport
Shopping on Sundays — most stores are closed (Ladenschlussgesetz)
Wishing someone happy birthday before their actual birthday — considered bad luck

safety.lgbtSafety: Very LGBTQ+ friendly. Same-sex marriage legal since 2017. Berlin is one of Europe's most LGBTQ+ inclusive cities. Cologne Pride (Christopher Street Day) is a major event.
safety.soloFemaleSafety: Very safe. Standard city precautions apply at night.
safety.notes: Germany is one of Europe's safest countries. Pickpockets operate in tourist areas (Cologne Cathedral, Berlin Hauptbahnhof, Munich Marienplatz). Keep bags zipped and close.

practical.visaFreeCountries: US citizens: 90 days visa-free (Schengen zone). UK citizens: 90 days in any 180-day period. ETA (ETIAS) system planned for 2025.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: May-September for outdoor activities and festivals (Oktoberfest late Sep-Oct). Christmas markets in December are magical. Avoid school holiday weeks for crowds.

immediate: Follow evacuation orders from local authorities (Katastrophenschutz)
Move vehicles and valuables to upper floors or high ground
Do not drive through flooded roads — floods can sweep vehicles away
after: Check structural safety before re-entering buildings
Follow THW (Federal Agency for Technical Relief) instructions

steps: File a police report immediately — get the report number, you will need it
Contact the US Embassy or nearest consulate: Contact the nearest US Embassy
Bring the police report + any ID you have (driver's license, copy of passport)
Apply for an Emergency Passport (usually issued within 1-2 business days)
Notify your travel insurance and airline of the situation
stolenPassport.notes: Keep a digital copy of your passport in cloud storage (Google Photos, iCloud) and email yourself a scan before travel.

steps: Go to the nearest police station (or call 110)
Bring ID or a copy of your passport if available
Request a written report — ask for an English copy or certified translation if needed
Keep the report number safe — required for insurance claims
For theft: list all stolen items with approximate values
policeReport.notes: In many countries, tourist police stations are available in major cities — they have English-speaking staff. Ask your hotel concierge for the nearest tourist police.

steps: If involved in an accident: do not move vehicles if anyone is injured
Call police (110) and ambulance (112) if there are injuries
Exchange contact, license, and insurance details with other parties
Document the scene with photos before moving vehicles
Contact your rental car company's emergency line
Contact your travel insurance's 24h assistance line
roadsideAssistance.notes: Traffic drives on the RIGHT. An International Driving Permit (IDP) is recommended for most foreign licenses. Rental vehicles are available at major airports and cities.
